THE CLAUSE

Instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority.

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

THE CLAIMS READ OUT OF IT

  C1 instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority
  C2 the chain-of-command principle is designed to maximize steerability and control for users and developers

EVERY SENTENCE THE TRANSLATION RENDERS BACK

  0. «the principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control»
  1. «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  2. «instruction I is assigned a level of authority L»
  3. «the authority level of instruction I is higher than the authority level of instruction J»
  4. P is «P is the chain-of-command principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority» when P is equal to «P is the chain-of-command principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority»
  5. clause l1_170_n040 obliges ⟨act override_instruction(I, J)⟩ when «instruction I is assigned a level of authority L» and «instruction I is assigned a level of authority L» and «the authority level of instruction I is higher than the authority level of instruction J»
